title: How Feeding Babies Works: The Breast
summary: Josh and Chuck open with a Sketch Fest promo in San Francisco, then start a two-part series on how feeding babies works, focusing on breastfeeding (Part one). They cover the stages of lactogenesis, colostrum and mature milk, the composition of breast milk (including oligosaccharides that feed the infant gut microbiome), foremilk and hindmilk, immunity transfer via saliva, benefits and their relative nature across countries, and the hormones oxytocin and prolactin and their bonding effects. They discuss latching and breastfeeding holds, difficulties and lactation consultants, supplementing with formula to avoid dehydration, induced lactation for adoptive or non-birth mothers, galactagogues, storage of expressed milk, diet and food sensitivities, alcohol and smoking, and the history of the La Leche League and the second-wave lactivism movement. They also cover US paid maternity leave and a 2015 deposition incident involving Donald Trump and attorney Elizabeth Beck. The episode ends with a sign-off and no listener mail.
topics: Donald Trump deposition breast pump incident

segments.title: Sketch Fest promo and show intro
segments.summary: Josh promotes a January Sketch Fest show in San Francisco, then the hosts introduce the episode and its two-part structure on feeding babies.

segments.title: Stages of breast milk production
segments.summary: The hosts describe lactogenesis stages, alveoli and lactocytes producing milk from the mother's nutrients, and how milk composition changes day to day.

segments.title: Colostrum, mature milk and infant digestion
segments.summary: Colostrum is described as the first thick golden milk for newborns, aiding passage of meconium. Mature milk's fat, minerals, vitamins, lactose and whey protein are covered, along with oligosaccharides that feed the infant's gut microbiome.

segments.title: Immunity transfer and foremilk/hindmilk
segments.summary: Babies' saliva during nursing can prompt the mother's body to produce targeted antibodies. The hosts explain foremilk and hindmilk, and note that exclusive breastfeeding is recommended for six months by WHO and AAP, with benefits relative to setting.

segments.title: Cost and convenience of breastfeeding
segments.summary: The hosts discuss savings on formula, the cost of pumps, and convenience compared with preparing formula and sterilizing bottles.

segments.title: Oxytocin, prolactin and the mother-infant bond
segments.summary: Prolactin drives milk production and oxytocin drives milk let-down. Oxytocin floods during labor and nursing, reorganizes maternal brain circuits, reduces stress, aids smell imprinting, and shifts maternal priorities. Skin-to-skin contact is recommended for all parents, and holding can support infant development even without breastfeeding.

segments.title: Latching, breastfeeding holds and practice
segments.summary: The hosts describe learning to breastfeed, the latch, and common holds including cradle, football and side-lying. They note breastfeeding takes practice and that milk may take days to come in.

segments.title: Breastfeeding difficulties, lactation help and formula supplementation
segments.summary: The hosts advise keeping nursing, seeing a lactation consultant, and avoiding judgmental mommy blogs. They warn that a doctor should be consulted so babies get enough calories, citing hypernatremic dehydration cases. They mention a podcast and discuss shame around formula and breastfeeding.

segments.title: Induced lactation, galactagogues and breastfeeding duration
segments.summary: Adoptive and non-birth mothers can sometimes induce lactation through hand massage, hand expression, and galactagogues such as metoclopramide and fenugreek. The hosts discuss recommended duration and introducing solids around six months.

segments.title: Storing breast milk and maternal diet
segments.summary: Storage times for expressed milk depend on fridge and freezer type. The hosts then discuss how maternal diet affects milk flavor, recommended extra calories, and foods that may cause gas or sensitivities, with an elimination diet suggestion.

segments.title: Alcohol, smoking, caffeine and drug exposure
segments.summary: The hosts explain that alcohol in breast milk tracks maternal blood alcohol and advise waiting about two hours, citing AAP guidance. They say nicotine lowers milk supply and vitamin C, and mention a case of cocaine passed through breast milk.

segments.title: History of formula and La Leche League lactivism
segments.summary: The hosts describe the mid-century shift toward formula and the rise of La Leche League, founded by Catholic mothers, and the second-wave lactivism inspired by Our Bodies, Ourselves. They discuss confounding factors in breastfeeding studies and WHO's 2007 review of claimed benefits.

segments.title: Paid maternity leave and workplace pumping
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the difficulty of breastfeeding while working, the US lack of federal paid maternity leave, and the FMLA's unpaid twelve weeks.

segments.title: Donald Trump deposition breast pump incident
segments.summary: Chuck recounts a deposition in which Donald Trump called attorney Elizabeth Beck disgusting when she pumped breast milk. Trump's counsel said the pumping was a stunt during the deposition, and the hosts comment that the word should not be used about breastfeeding women.

segments.title: Closing and sign-off
segments.summary: Josh previews part two and gives the show's social media and website contact details. No listener mail is read.
